A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FIMP and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Shared methods and experiments can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original brain-signal, gene-expression, and CIFAR-100 reconstruction results, plus appendix node-classification experiments and attention analyses.

after.justification: v5 reports original reconstruction, cell-type classification, Mapillary classification, and zero-shot embedding results, alongside retained biological attention analyses.

M1.justification: Node tokenization, destination-query/source-key-value cross-attention, message aggregation, and reuse of pretrained attention weights remain the core procedure. FIMP-base renames the original unpretrained variant. Expanded equations, pseudocode, and evaluation modes do not establish a substantive new method component.

E1.justification: v5 replaces synthetic CIFAR-100 image reconstruction with Mapillary country classification and adds cell-type classification on mouse hippocampus and newly introduced SeqFISH mouse embryo data. It removes Cora, Pubmed, and Amazon Computers classification and the OGBN-arXiv attention study. Biological reconstruction datasets remain.

E2.justification: v5 Tables 2–3 add standalone scGPT and ViT comparisons, directly comparing FIMP with foundation models without graph inputs. Its zero-shot comparison also includes a majority-class baseline. Removing v3 Table 4 eliminates comparisons with DGI, GRACE, BGRL, DeepWalk, raw features, and a randomly initialized GCN. Comparator membership in the retained reconstruction comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported fMRI settings change from 400 to 320 timepoints and from mean/standard-deviation normalization to median/interquartile-range scaling. For limited human-heart reconstruction, the stated dataset changes from 1,000 to 200 cells and FIMP samples 50 rather than 30 genes. v5 also introduces image-classification protocols and a zero-shot evaluation using 400 embeddings with a 75/25 linear-classifier split. These documentation changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds analysis of transfer without graph-specific training and foundation-only controls relevant to the benefit of graph integration. It removes the full-versus-limited-data/masking comparison and citation-network word-attention case study. The out-of-domain ViT control and biological attention case studies were already present; the brain and gene attention figures are unchanged.

E5.justification: Retained reconstruction tables continue to report five-run results with ± uncertainty values. Added classification tables follow the same uncertainty-display practice, without documenting a new run-count policy, seed protocol, uncertainty estimator, or significance test.

E6.justification: v5 adds cell-type and Mapillary classification results, including FIMP-ViT accuracy of 63.2% after finetuning and 40.6% for a linear classifier using zero-shot embeddings. CIFAR-100, standard node-classification, and full-data gene results disappear. v5 Table 1 numerically matches v3 Table 2's limited-data block, and v5 Table 4 matches v3 Table 1 despite revised setting descriptions; these are not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v5 Section 2.2 adds explicit mathematical definitions of GAT attention scores and normalized coefficients in Equations 3–4. The underlying FIMP attention and aggregation mathematics remains equivalent, with no new theorem, proof, or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The central foundation-model adaptation claim remains, but v5 explicitly focuses it on non-textual models and promotes competitive zero-shot graph embeddings to a primary contribution. v3's abstract, introduction, and conclusion did not claim this zero-shot capability. v5 also explicitly claims the first broad exploration of non-textual foundation models for graph tasks.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly limits its validation to image and biological data and identifies multimodal and heterogeneous graphs as unresolved extensions. It removes v3's bag-of-words applicability discussion and citation-attention interpretations. Explanations based on tokenization, domain-aligned pretraining, and the biological attention studies remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 removes v3 Appendix A.7's exact parameter counts, epochs, learning rates, dropout, and weight-decay tables, along with explicit matched-budget, GraphSAINT, and scheduler descriptions. It adds the scGPT checkpoint identity, foundation-model sizes and layer counts, Flash Attention usage, image preprocessing details, and spatial-data filtering/split information, and documents 24GB GPUs. Substantial reproducibility information is both added and lost.

R1.justification: v5 substantially refocuses positioning around feature-level cross-node attention and non-textual foundation models. It adds comparisons with One-for-All and Talk Like a Graph and expands attention-based graph literature through works including GTN, Graph-BERT, SAN, and Graphormer. Much of v3's general foundation-model and contrastive graph-learning review is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v5 adds an explicit contribution list and dedicated preliminaries, moves related work to Appendix C, reorders experiments, and reorganizes the appendix into sections A–D. Authorship presentation and variant terminology also change.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn, and v5 adds a performance-summary chart and classification tables. The citation-attention figure, standard node-classification table, and hyperparameter tables are removed; the gene-results table loses its full/limited structure. Biological attention figures are retained and renumbered. The author block and overall page layout are substantially redesigned.

improvement.justification: New comparisons against standalone scGPT and ViT, a real-world image graph, and clearer exposition strengthen evaluation of the central contribution. However, v5 reports identical reconstruction scores under materially revised protocol descriptions and removes exact training configurations from v3 Appendix A.7. The PDFs do not explain the relationship between those scores and revised settings. These gains and unresolved losses in experimental traceability prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
